# QS-CFW-7189-64 — Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (52100)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-7189-64

## Scope
This quality specification defines metallurgical and dimensional acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 manufactured from 52100 steel at Plant P1. It applies to finished forgings released for heat treatment and final machining and to any subcontracted processing that affects hardness or bore geometry. The intent is to ensure functional interchangeability and service life expectations for assemblies using CFW-7189-64.

Background and rationale: bearing rings are functionally sensitive to core hardness and bore geometry. The specified hardness range controls through-hardened microstructure and residual austenite, while the bore diameter tolerance controls fit and assembly performance. The maximum forging weight constraint limits handling and process capacity within Plant P1 equipment.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness, bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) | 24-29 HRC | Measured on forged and finished surface per Inspection Method below |
| Bore diameter tolerance, bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) | ±0.04 mm | Applies after final machining and before assembly |
| Maximum forging weight, bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) | 22.9 kg | Includes any attached mandrels or temporary fixtures during handling |

Notes on the table: Each row describes an acceptance criterion that must be met before a part is released from final inspection. The hardness requirement is a control on heat treat and quench practice; the bore tolerance is a geometry control for final machining; the maximum forging weight is an equipment and handling constraint.

## Inspection method
General approach: Inspectors shall verify each requirement using calibrated equipment and documented procedures. Calibration of instruments must be traceable and records retained.

Hardness verification:
- Take hardness measurements at representative locations around the ring cross-section, avoiding radiused corners and machining marks. Use a Rockwell C tester suitable for hardened steels.
- The hardness requirement is: The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) is 24-29 HRC.
- Document each individual reading and the location on the part drawing where it was taken. Report the highest and lowest readings per part together with the part identifier and inspector.

Bore diameter verification:
- Inspect the bore after final internal machining using a bore gauge or calibrated plug gauge system appropriate to the bore size. Measure concentricity and roundness as required by drawing control features.
- The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) is ±0.04 mm.
- Record the measured nominal diameter and deviation from nominal. Include measurement equipment ID and calibration date.

Maximum forging weight verification:
- Confirm that the forging batch weight does not exceed factory handling limits by weighing the forging after cooling and removal from dies or fixtures.
- The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) is 22.9 kg.
- If the forging is attached to mandrels or fixtures at weighing, include those items in the reported weight and note their identity.

Sampling and frequency:
- Inspect each lot at receiving inspection and again prior to final release. For multi-piece lots, follow plant sampling rules verified in process control documents. Record sampling rationale in the inspection record.

Equipment and calibration:
- Use calibrated instruments with current calibration labels. Calibration records shall be available for audit. List of equipment used, calibration due status, and inspector signature must be entered in the inspection record for each lot.

Examples of acceptable records:
- A hardness report showing individual readings taken at documented locations, part identifiers, date, and inspector name.
- A dimensional report listing bore measurements, measurement device IDs, calibration dates, and the resulting pass/fail for the ±0.04 mm tolerance.
- A weight ticket from a calibrated scale indicating the forging mass including fixtures, with inspector initials.

## Nonconformance handling
Identification and containment:
- Any part failing to meet a stated requirement shall be identified as nonconforming, segregated from conforming material, and tagged with a nonconformance notice. Include the failed characteristic, measured values, and inspector identity in the notice.

Disposition options and evaluation:
- Evaluate nonconforming items for repair, rework, or scrap based on root cause and feasibility. Rework proposals must include specific steps to bring the part into compliance without compromising metallurgical properties or geometry and must be reviewed by engineering.
- Example dispositions: localized machining if geometry permits, or scrapping if the structural integrity or metallurgical state cannot be restored. For hardness-related failures, engineering must assess whether heat treatment can correct the condition without introducing new risks.

Documentation and approval:
- All nonconformance records must detail the corrective action or disposition decision, the approver’s name and title, and any instructions for re-inspection. Retain records with the lot history.

Corrective action and preventive measures:
- For recurrent nonconformance, perform a root cause analysis and implement process changes. Document corrective action plans and effectiveness checks. Record training or process adjustments taken to prevent recurrence.

Records to keep
- Inspection reports for hardness, bore diameter, and weight for each lot.
- Calibration certificates for all measurement devices used.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition approvals.
- Any engineering evaluations or corrective action records associated with disposition or process changes.

Retention and access
- Maintain records in the document control system associated with QS-CFW-7189-64. Records shall be available for internal audit and customer review as required by contract.

End of document.
